newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX to allow delivery of Cusiana from July 97.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX to allow delivery of Cusiana from July 97.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) said Wednesday that it will allow delivery of Colombian Cusiana crude against its light, sweet crude futures starting with the July, 1997 contract.

NYMEX said it will apply to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) for permission and also request approval to adjust the premiums and discounts applied to the foreign crudes delivered against the contract.
Currently, a buyer recieves a 30 cents per barrel discount on delivery of Brent, Forties and Oseberg and pays a 60 cents per barrel premium for delivery of Bonny Light.
The proposed differentials include 30 cent discounts for Brent and Oseberg, 35 cent discount for Forties, a 40 cent premium for Bonny Light and a 15 cent premium for delivery of Cusiana crude.

NYMEX president Patrick Thompson said that "these amendments ensure that the exchange's benchmark light, sweet crude oil futures contract will retain its role as an accurate and reliable global price reference for the world's most actively traded physical commodity."
